questions.prompt: The workspace is /work/app. Why does minidsh not use `target.startsWith(root)` to decide if a path is writable?
options: It is too slow for long paths
It would allow /work/app-secrets/key, which only shares the same starting letters
It fails for files that do not exist yet
questions.explanation: '/work/app-secrets/key' starts with '/work/app' as text but lies outside it. Computing the relative path gives '../app-secrets/key', which climbs out and is refused.

questions.prompt: On a Mac you put '/tmp' in the list without resolving it. What happens when a command writes /tmp/out.txt?
options: The write is allowed, because the spelling matches
The write goes to the working folder instead
The write is refused, because the kernel compares the real name /private/tmp
questions.explanation: /tmp is a link to /private/tmp, and the enforcement compares resolved paths. A grant spelled /tmp matches nothing, which is why every root is resolved first.

questions.prompt: Why must the write and edit tools check the same list as shell commands?
options: They run inside the harness's own process, which the kernel fence does not cover
The model is not allowed to call them otherwise
The list is needed to find the file to edit
questions.explanation: The kernel fence applies to separate programs the harness starts. File tools run in-process, so without the same check the model could write by another route what the shell refused.
